The biggest threat may emerge from recent Thirsk third Beerwah, while C&D winner Startling sits on an attractive mark and cannot be dismissed either.

C&D winner Front Gunner got back on the scoresheet at Redcar 42 days ago and should make his presence felt once more, along with Bantz, who will enjoy this sounder surface.

And Gladiadora is yet to win in seven career runs; she has placed on a few occasions, therefore she will have to settle for that here once again.

selections.comment: A lot of these have been running for years and have loads of experience under their belts; however, HARDLASS is the opposite of that and has only run ten times. She is yet to win in those ten starts; however, she has finished second on two occasions this season for her new yard, in just three runs for them. A 2nd at this venue back in May, qualifying her for this race, before going on to slightly disappoint at Bath again, she did bounce back to some sort of form, however, when coming 2nd at Ffos-Las last time out, only just getting denied by a nose. She deserves to get her head in front, and this could be the race that she does that. Rogue Endeavour is another one who is yet to win, but he has been creeping down the weights lately and has run well on a few occasions this season; he can claim a very decent 2nd spot here. And Neptune Legend has run plenty of times in his career, winning on six occasions; however, he might not be the force of old, therefore he will have to settle with filling the places here.

selections.comment: A further step up in trip for the Sir Mark Prescott horse LAUNCESTON could mean he finally gets his head in front at the sixth time of asking after a decent 2nd at this venue last time out on his first run since the gelding operation. This is his second run since that op; therefore, he is entitled to come on for the run here, and with the further trip surely going to suit him, he could get off the mark here before improving even more by going on a winning spree for a yard that does so well with these types. The yard is in decent form at present, and so is Luke Morris, who is currently operating at a 21% win strike rate for the last 14 days. Offiah's Boy was a nice enough winner at this venue a few weeks back; he has since disappointed at Windsor, but now coming back here, he can bounce back to some sort of form and claim 2nd spot. And Virtual Hug was slightly unlucky last time out when he got boxed in at a crucial part of the race; he was travelling well then and did respond late on, running on well, but it was too little too late. He can run into a place again here.

selections.comment: A very competitive renewal with some real speedsters in the field, so a fine spectacle is in prospect too. Asfoora is probably the likeliest winner as her best form - crucially (and unlike some key rivals), at 5f - gives her a good chance but she is short enough in the betting considering that she wasn't quite at her peak back in Britain last time. She may well be sharper now and obviously has to be respected but it makes sense to cast around instead for a bigger-priced each-way alternative. That brings in KHAADEM, who is two from two here (including in this race in 2022), was still up to winning a Gr 1 last season (albeit at 6f) and who showed plenty of zip on last month's return until lack of race fitness seemed to catch him out. Frost At Dawn was second in a Gr 1 last time and may claim minor honours while up-and-coming 3yo Town And Country is another one for the shortlist, as are Big Mojo and Time For Sandals after recent heroics in 6f Gr 1s.

selections.comment: A very trappy race with some hugely promising sorts. AEOLIAN and Participle both recieve 7lb from the three previous winners in the field and that may prove the edge. Participle made a hugely promising debut last term when going down by a nose and would just about set the standard on that. However, his comeback run, when a heavily supported favourite, was dismal with no obvious excuse. If bouncing back he should go close but it's a significant 'if' and Aeolian looks the more solid option. William Haggas's filly was a length second on debut over this trip and should take a big step forward for it. Of the trio of last time out winners, all of which pose a serious threat, La Scanderbeide looks best placed to defy the penalty and land the double having powered home on debut at yarmouth over a mile. The step up to 1m2f should be well within her compass and she's entitled to be bang there at the finish

selections.comment: A chance is taken that CHARMING FELLOW can leave his comeback run behind and return to the sort of levels that saw him land a class 5 nursery in October on 5th start off 56. He's gone off favourite on his last three starts and when things drop right looks capable of delivering off this kind of mark. Dashing Donkey is undoubtedly a more solid alternative but less rewarding. William Stone's gelding won over course and distance last time and while a 7lb rise won't be easy to defy he has doubled up before and is entitled to go close again. Optimatum is steadily progressing and although turned over at odds-on last time is in good spirits and should go well in first time cheekpieces and can reach the frame ahead of the promising Left Over Love, who may just find her stamina ebbing away late on

Newyorkstateofmind is another who has dropped in the weights but shown he retains some of his ability so he could complete the tricast.

selections.comment: Willie Mullins holds a strong hand bidding to follow up last year's success. Uncle Pat looks the first string on jockey bookings having finished runner up over further on chase debut on his first start since the autumn last time. He should build on that and holds fair claims but it is his stablemate JARRIVE DE MEE who appeals most. He lost his unbeaten record over hurdles at the top level last time but lost nothing in defeat and is open to plenty of progress now chasing. This track will suit his style and if getting into a rhythm he should be tough to catch. The standard is set by Sandor Clegane who brings in some strong Grade 1 form from last spring and has been in decent form over hurdles this year. However his finishing effort often leaves plenty to be desired so he may have to make do with a place.

selections.comment: Last year's winner TAIPAN is hugely respected as he's versatile ground wise and has proved he retained his ability on his penultimate start. However he could be vulnerable to a slightly classier rival and COLONIA VICTORIA could fit that bill. Her German Group form arguably sets the standard in this sphere and she is open to improvement for her new yard having already taken a hurdle in impressive fashion in the spring. Bunting has proven frustrating in both codes for Willie Mullins given his market support but his Grade 1 juvenile form suggests that there is more to come in this sphere.

Tassarolo has enjoyed success in both codes of late and his hurdles victory suggests this longer trip could deliver more on the flat. Pralognan seeks a hat trick over both codes and remains well treated on his French form so completes the list of dangers.
